X.why: 'Midnight at the edge of Spain' frames Gibraltar as Spain's edge, which is fine, but the pitch leads with the new treaty and the border, which reads like a modern political hook. The 'Only five changed who ruled it' line sounds like a British-leaning take that the sieges mostly failed. The only sources named are Sayer (a British historian) and the Gibraltar National Museum, so the sourcing is entirely British. 'Told from both sides' records' is a promise with no Spanish source shown.
X.moment_you_would_leave_or_doubt: The title card with only Sayer 1862 and the Gibraltar National Museum as sources, followed by 'told from both sides' records'. That claim isn't backed up, and the next minute will probably cast the Spanish attackers as the failed aggressors.

Y.why: It opens with a Spanish historian (Montero, 1860) before the British one and quotes them side by side, so Spain is not just the attacker in the story. The title card names Sayer and García Sanz together, which makes 'both sides' believable. It leaves out the UK–EU treaty politics and the 'only five changed hands' framing, so it feels like history rather than a verdict. The 'key of the Mediterranean' motif is neutral and explains why everyone wanted it.
Y.moment_you_would_leave_or_doubt: A slight doubt at 'this key' being fought over with no mention yet of who actually owns it today or of Utrecht, but I would stay at least until the 1704 section to see how it treats the British capture and Spain's claim.

Z.why: It is neutral and factual, 'the Gibraltar frontier' and 'to walk in from Spain', and it lists García Sanz alongside Sayer, so the sources are balanced. It has no editorial line and gives no Spanish voice up front, so it is less engaging than Y. It also drops the 'edge of Spain' phrasing, which I would have noticed.
Z.moment_you_would_leave_or_doubt: 'Since July 2026, this gate has had no routine checks' sits oddly without context, and I would doubt whether the video pushes a treaty-friendly, pro-status-quo angle. The two-minute mark would decide it if no Spanish narrator or source appears.

one_change_to_the_best_version: Keep the Montero and Sayer quotes, but add one early line that names the Spanish claim and the British possession plainly, for example 'Spain ceded it at Utrecht in 1713 and has contested it since', so the neutrality is stated and not just implied.
